Aerospace NDT training in East Hartford: the short answer

Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based aerospace NDT training for East Hartford and Connecticut River valley employers and technicians. Theory is taught live online and practicals run onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Because the corridor is built around jet engines, the focus is on the methods engine hardware depends on: high-sensitivity fluorescent penetrant, eddy current on rotating and machined parts, and ultrasonic inspection of forgings and bar stock, along with radiography, magnetic particle and visual testing at Levels I and II, plus Level III preparation. Engine OEMs and their suppliers certify under NAS 410. Our training supports those written practices and does not replace them.

East Hartford is a jet-engine town, and engine NDT is its own discipline. Airframe inspection is mostly about large structures and fastened joints. Engine inspection is about rotating parts (discs, shafts, blades, cases) where a small, undetected crack can have serious consequences, so penetrant sensitivity, eddy current scanning and the ultrasonic quality of the original forging or billet carry exceptional weight. That's why "aerospace NDT training East Hartford" deserves an answer about engines, and about the supplier network that feeds them, rather than a generic aerospace page.

Atlantis has no training centre in East Hartford or anywhere in Connecticut. We teach theory live online and bring practicals to the employer, on its own penetrant line, eddy current scanners, ultrasonic immersion or contact systems, and reference standards. For engine work that's the only sensible way to run a practical, because the part families, techniques and acceptance criteria are programme-specific.

Aerospace NDT work in East Hartford and the Connecticut corridor

  • Jet engines. Pratt & Whitney is headquartered in East Hartford. It produces military engines there, including the F135 that powers all three F-35 variants, with work also at Middletown, and supports commercial engine programmes. Engine production and overhaul call for fluorescent penetrant at high sensitivity on machined and finished hardware, eddy current inspection of features such as bolt holes, slots and edges on rotating parts, ultrasonic inspection of forgings and bar stock, and radiography of castings.
  • Aerospace systems. Collins Aerospace, operating at Windsor Locks as the successor to Hamilton Sundstrand, makes aerospace systems and components that need production NDT on machined, cast and forged parts.
  • Helicopters. Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, has its main plant in Stratford. Rotorcraft structure and dynamic components bring their own inspection demands and add to the state's aerospace NDT labour market.
  • The supplier network. Hundreds of Connecticut machine shops, forging and casting houses, heat treaters, coating and plating shops and component repair stations work to engine and airframe flow-downs. Many run NDT under Nadcap accreditation or buy it from accredited labs. This is where outside training, written-practice help and Level III support are most often needed.

Connecticut also has major naval shipbuilding at Groton, which works to separate Navy NDT requirements. That's covered on NDT training in Groton. Industrial and fabrication NDT in the Hartford area is covered on our general NDT training page for East Hartford.

Aerospace NDT methods for East Hartford work, and the specifications behind them

This is context, not a substitute for your customer's specifications. Engine OEM process specifications, purchase orders and your written practice decide what applies.

MethodEngine and aerospace application in the corridorTypical code / standard
Fluorescent penetrant (PT)Final inspection of machined engine parts, blades, vanes, cases and fittings; overhaul inspection after cleaningASTM E1417, AMS 2644 materials (sensitivity levels), OEM process specs
Eddy current (ET)Surface and near-surface crack detection on rotating parts, bolt holes and slots; conductivity checks; inspection in overhaulOEM process specifications, SAE ARP4402, ASTM E1004
Ultrasonic (UT), contact and immersionForging, bar and billet inspection for internal discontinuities; thickness checks; inspection of welded and bonded partsAMS 2630 / AMS 2631 family where specified, ASTM E2375, OEM specs
Phased array UT (PAUT)Higher-coverage inspection of forgings and welds where the OEM has qualified the techniqueOEM-qualified techniques
Radiography / digital radiography (RT)Castings such as cases and structural castings, welded assemblies, internal passage checksASTM E1742, OEM specs
Magnetic particle (MT)Steel shafts, gears and fittings at suppliers and overhaul shopsASTM E1444, OEM specs
Visual (VT)Every stage, including borescope inspection of assembled enginesOEM and employer procedures

East Hartford method spotlight: penetrant and eddy current on rotating parts. For engine hardware, the inspection that matters most is often the one that looks simplest. High-sensitivity fluorescent penetrant only works if surface preparation, dwell, removal, developer and viewing conditions are controlled exactly, and most rejected audits trace back to process control rather than technician eyesight. Eddy current on bolt holes, slots and edges of rotating parts depends on probe selection, frequency, reference standards and disciplined scanning. Our PT and ET courses put weight on process control, reference standards and the documentation an engine-programme auditor will check, and onsite practicals use your own line and standards. See penetrant testing in aviation, eddy current testing in aviation, the PT Level II course and the ET Level II course.

Which certification scheme East Hartford aerospace employers expect

Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only. The other schemes are listed so you know what Connecticut employers ask for.

SchemeWho requires it in the corridorDoes Atlantis SNT-TC-1A training fit?
NAS 410 / EN 4179Engine, systems and rotorcraft OEMs and the suppliers they flow requirements down toPartly. The method theory overlaps, and some NAS 410 written practices accept outside formal training after Responsible Level 3 review. Certification and examinations stay with the employer. Ask first.
Nadcap NDT (AC7114)Suppliers whose engine and airframe customers require accredited NDTOur training records are built to be traceable at audit. The accreditation is the supplier's.
Engine OEM supplier approvalsSuppliers doing NDT on engine hardware, often with OEM-specific technique approvals on top of NAS 410No. These are OEM-controlled. Training builds the foundation, and the approvals come through the employer.
FAA Part 145 repair-station programmesComponent and engine repair stationsOften yes, as formal training where the station's manual permits.
ASNT SNT-TC-1ASome suppliers, tooling and equipment makers, and the region's industrial NDT employersYes. This is the scheme our courses are built on.
NAVSEA (T9074-AS-GIB-010/271)Naval shipbuilding work elsewhere in ConnecticutNo. It's a separate Navy certification and isn't offered.

See NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A for the full comparison. At a NAS 410 employer, your Responsible Level 3 controls your path, and outside training is most useful for method depth and exam readiness. At an SNT-TC-1A employer, our courses map directly onto the written practice.

The SNT-TC-1A certification path, step by step

Recommended minimum training and experience for each method and level are in the NDT training requirements matrix. Aerospace written practices commonly require more.

  1. Identify the written practice that will certify you, and any customer or OEM requirements layered on it.
  2. Complete formal training for the method and level, keeping the outline, hours, dates and instructor record.
  3. Build documented experience under certified personnel, logged and verified as you go.
  4. Pass the general examination on method principles.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the employer's equipment, procedures and specifications.
  6. Pass the practical examination on real specimens: cracked reference parts, penetrant panels, notched eddy current standards.
  7. Pass the vision examination, with near vision repeated at least annually.
  8. Receive written certification from the employer.
  9. Recertify at the interval the written practice sets.

More: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Radiation licensing, export control and access in Connecticut

Connecticut became the 40th NRC Agreement State, with state authority over most radioactive materials taking effect on 30 September 2025. Before that, the NRC licensed radioactive materials in Connecticut directly. Radioactive-materials licensing, including industrial radiography sources, now sits with the Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) Radiation Division, which also registers X-ray equipment. Most engine radiography uses X-ray in shielded facilities. If your company held an NRC licence, check the transition arrangements with DEEP. Radiation-safety training and radiographer qualification are separate from NDT method certification.

Military engine programmes involve export-controlled technical data, so engine-related NDT roles can be limited to US persons, and the employer decides who may see controlled parts and procedures. Onsite practical sessions are planned around what the employer clears for training. Plant access is employer-controlled and badge-based.

See the statewide NDT consulting in Connecticut hub, steel NDT consulting in Hartford for fabrication work, and power NDT consulting in Bridgeport. Book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods across five virtual environments, including an aircraft hangar, so they can rehearse set-up, scanning and evaluation before real hardware. It's for practice only and doesn't replace the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, onsite practicals and examination administration for the SNT-TC-1A programmes we support.

Frequently asked questions about aerospace NDT training in East Hartford

Where can I get aerospace NDT training in East Hartford?

The large engine and systems employers train in-house under NAS 410, and Connecticut Aero Tech covers NDT within aviation maintenance. Atlantis delivers SNT-TC-1A-based training with live online theory and onsite practicals at your employer's facility. We have no classroom in Connecticut. Ask us about dates and delivery.

What NDT methods do jet engine manufacturers use?

Mainly high-sensitivity fluorescent penetrant, eddy current on rotating parts and machined features, ultrasonic inspection of forgings and bar stock, radiography of castings, and visual and borescope inspection. Magnetic particle covers steel parts.

Which method should I learn first for engine NDT work in Connecticut?

Fluorescent penetrant is the usual first method. It's used on almost every machined engine part, and it teaches the process-control habits engine work demands. Eddy current is the most valuable second method because it's used heavily on rotating parts. Ultrasonic inspection of forgings and bar stock tends to come later, often at forging and material suppliers rather than on final-inspection lines.

Is production NDT different from engine overhaul NDT?

Yes. Production inspection checks new parts against drawing and process specifications on a controlled line. Overhaul inspection examines used parts after cleaning and has to tell service damage, such as fatigue cracks, erosion and corrosion, apart from acceptable wear, working from the engine manual and repair limits. The methods are the same, but the judgement calls and documentation are different. Training for each should reflect that.

Can Atlantis certify me to NAS 410?

No. NAS 410 certification is issued by your employer under its written practice and Responsible Level 3. Some written practices accept outside formal training, so check with your employer first.

Can I take aerospace NDT training online in Connecticut?

The theory, yes, live and instructor-led. Practical training and the practical exam need real equipment and specimens, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility.

How long does penetrant or eddy current Level II take?

It depends on prior certifications and the written practice. Minimum training and experience vary by method and level, and engine-programme written practices often set more. See the training requirements matrix, then confirm with your employer.

What does aerospace NDT training cost in East Hartford?

We quote on request. The price depends on methods, levels, number of technicians, whether practicals run onsite, and any written-practice or Level III support. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a quote.

Who regulates industrial radiography in Connecticut now?

Since Connecticut became an NRC Agreement State on 30 September 2025, the DEEP Radiation Division licenses most radioactive materials, including radiography sources, and it also registers X-ray equipment. Radiographers must meet the radiation-safety requirements separately from NDT certification.

Is ASNT SNT-TC-1A accepted by Connecticut aerospace suppliers?

Some smaller suppliers and non-aerospace employers certify under SNT-TC-1A. Suppliers to the engine and airframe OEMs usually work under NAS 410 flow-down. Your prior SNT-TC-1A records can shorten the bridge, but the new employer still certifies you.

Can I use GI Bill or WIOA funding for this training?

Those programmes require approved providers: VA approval for GI Bill benefits, and the state's eligible training provider list for WIOA through American Job Centers. Atlantis doesn't claim either approval, so check with the VA or your local American Job Center. Employer-funded training is the common alternative.

Can you train on our own penetrant line and eddy current standards?

Yes. Onsite practicals use your equipment, procedures and reference standards. Ask about onsite training for your East Hartford crew.

Do you prepare technicians for ASNT Level III?

Yes. We offer Basic and method preparation for experienced Level IIs. See ASNT Level III training, the Basic exam guide and the UT Level 2 practice questions.
